targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-961 (2026-08-29) is a genuine but low-powered negative for MECH-144 and SHOULD be scored, despite carrying non_degenerate: false. IT IS NOT SCORED TODAY: the indexer's non-degeneracy gate (build_experiment_indexes.py:3431) currently excludes it, and claim_evidence.v1.json shows MECH-144 scoring_excluded='degenerate'. Making this run count requires AMENDING the manifest flag and REBUILDING THE INDEX -- see this target's operative_action; fixing the driver bug alone only fixes future runs. That flag is a FALSE POSITIVE caused by a driver bug: at line 596 the driver builds geom_dist_groups = [[r['distance_std']] for ...], i.e. a list of SINGLETON groups, and passes it to metric_groups_are_degenerate, the WITHIN-group variant intended for multi-value groups such as [arm_on, arm_off] per seed. A singleton list has spread = max - min = 0 <= eps (1e-9) by definition, so every group is 'pinned' unconditionally and the check would fire identically on a perfect run. The readiness it purports to test is in fact sound: 32 active centers (floor 4) and distance_std 1.2100 / 1.0938 / 1.0408 (floor 0.5), all far above the 1e-6 degeneracy floor. On the substance, C1 (Pearson r of harm-discriminative valence against hazard proximity) measured -0.1937 / 0.1523 / 0.2150 against a pre-registered 0.35, passing 0/3 seeds with one negative. C2 (ablated null) carries no discriminative weight and the driver says so: ARM_ABLATED's evaluate_valence 'returns identically zero by construction', r is defined as 0.0 by the guarded helper, and C2 is 'recorded as a sanity check on the harness rather than a novel discriminative claim'. C1 is therefore the sole load-bearing criterion, and at 3 seeds this is a weak negative -- does_not_support at this scale and design, not a refutation.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: Give metric_groups_are_degenerate an arity guard so singleton groups cannot report as pinned
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: metric_is_degenerate returns on spread <= eps BEFORE the floor check, so a singleton group (max == min, spread 0) is unconditionally 'pinned' and no floor value can rescue it. metric_groups_are_degenerate therefore returns degenerate for ANY list of singletons, including on a perfect run. Refuse or warn on a group of size < 2 and point the caller at the flat metric_is_degenerate variant, which is what a per-seed scalar actually needs.

cluster_pattern.shape: Both runs carry non_degenerate: false AND emit a claim-weighting evidence_direction of does_not_support. The two underlying causes are OPPOSITE: V3-EXQ-960's degeneracy flag is true and correct (a real representation collapse, 2x-78x below its own pre-registered floor); V3-EXQ-961's is a false positive from a singleton-group driver bug.
cluster_pattern.structural_property: CORRECTED after red-team (verdict CONTESTED). The first revision asserted that 'the non-degeneracy net is COMPUTED and RECORDED but NOT WIRED to evidence_direction' and that nothing downstream prevents a degenerate run from weighing against a claim. THAT IS FALSE. build_experiment_indexes.py:3431-3436 implements the documented 2026-06-11 non-degeneracy gate (scoring_excluded = 'degenerate'), and it has ALREADY FIRED ON BOTH RUNS -- the live claim_evidence.v1.json shows MECH-143 and MECH-144 both scoring_excluded='degenerate' right now. The gate exists; it simply sits one layer downstream (at the indexer) of where the first revision looked (the drivers). What the two runs actually share is therefore NOT one missing coupling but a common CONSEQUENCE of a working gate fed by an unvalidated flag: because the gate is purely mechanical and trusts non_degenerate unconditionally, the flag's CORRECTNESS is load-bearing, and neither driver validates the input it computes that flag from. 960 sets it correctly and is correctly excluded; 961 sets it wrongly and is wrongly excluded. Calling this ONE structural property overstates it -- these are two genuinely independent defects (a real collapse vs a bad argument to a helper) that meet only at the shared downstream consumer.
